crossRefs.note: “The King will answer them, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers…
Moab was very afraid of the people, because they were many. Moab was distressed because of the children of Israel.
Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. He sent and called Balaam the son of Beor…
but I would not listen to Balaam; therefore he blessed you still. So I delivered you out of his hand.
How shall I curse whom God has not cursed? How shall I defy whom Yahweh has not defied?
He took up his parable, and said, “Rise up, Balak, and hear! Listen to me, you son of Zippor.
How goodly are your tents, Jacob, and your dwellings, Israel!
Nevertheless Yahweh your God wouldn’t listen to Balaam, but Yahweh your God turned the curse into a blessing to you…
They may curse, but you bless. When they arise, they will be shamed, but your servant shall rejoice.
My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him from Shittim to…

parallels.note: because they didn’t meet you with bread and with water on the way when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired…

people.name: Balaam
people.line: A prophet hired to curse Israel but blessed them instead.

people.name: Israel
people.line: Patriarch, son of Isaac, father of twelve tribes

translations.web: because they didn’t meet the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, to curse them; however our God turned the curse into a blessing.
translations.bsb: because they had not met the Israelites with food and water, but had hired Balaam to call down a curse against them (although our God had turned the curse into a blessing).
translations.kjv: Because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, that he should curse them: howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing.
translations.asv: because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, to curse them: howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing.
